entries.name: Seasonal Work Is Ending
entries.summary:
The harvest, fishing season, caravan season, festival circuit, construction period, shipping window, hunting season, or other work cycle you rely on is ending.

Narrative effects: You have learned to negotiate for what comes next and think geographically about where another season of work might be available.

entries.name: Sent Away from Home
entries.summary:
Someone with influence over your life sent you away from home for work, protection, discipline, education, politics, family convenience, or another reason you did not fully choose.

Narrative effects: Being relocated made routes and unfamiliar customs immediate adult concerns without determining why you were sent away.

entries.name: Shop Is Failing
entries.summary:
A shop or small business you own, help run, depend on, or expect to inherit is losing money, customers, suppliers, stock, or relevance.

Narrative effects: Commercial trouble has made prices, stock quality, margins, and difficult negotiations immediate concerns.

entries.name: Someone Depends on Your Income
entries.summary:
Another person's ordinary needs substantially depend on the money or resources you bring in.

Narrative effects: Knowing someone else relies on your earnings has made consistent work and practical negotiation much harder to treat casually.

entries.name: Someone Owes You Money
entries.summary:
Another person, business, employer, companion, client, or associate owes you money that you increasingly need returned.

Narrative effects: Trying to collect has taught you both how to negotiate repayment and how to learn whether someone genuinely cannot pay or simply does not intend to.

entries.name: Stuck Where You Started
entries.summary:
Adult life has begun to feel uncomfortably similar to the life you expected to outgrow. The same streets, routines, work, people, or limitations are still around you, and you are increasingly aware that nothing will change simply because time passes.

Narrative effects: You are practiced at continuing through repetitive circumstances while paying close attention to how other people found, missed, or created opportunities to move forward.

entries.name: Sailor Adult
entries.summary:
You worked aboard ships, barges, ferries, fishing vessels, merchant craft, patrol boats, or river transports during early adulthood.

Narrative effects: Your balance adjusts before your mind remembers the floor should be still.

entries.name: Scholar's Assistant
entries.summary:
You worked as a scholar's assistant, copying notes, sorting texts, preparing references, carrying books, reading aloud, cataloging findings, or chasing facts others considered too small.

Narrative effects: You ask for dates, sources, copies, and who funded the research.

entries.name: Scout for Hire
entries.summary:
You sold your eyes, feet, and caution as a scout for caravans, patrols, expeditions, militias, hunters, or adventuring parties. You learned that returning with information matters more than looking heroic.

Narrative effects: You look ahead for danger before anyone finishes discussing the route.

entries.name: Seasonal Laborer
entries.summary:
Your work followed the season rather than a permanent position. Planting, harvest, shearing, fishing runs, timber work, livestock drives, repairs, road work, and other temporary labor carried you from one stretch of hard work to the next.

Narrative effects: You think of the year in workloads, weather, short opportunities, and the jobs that disappear once the season turns.

entries.name: Shipwright's Hand
entries.summary:
You work in a shipyard, drydock, riverside yard, or repair crew helping build and maintain hulls, frames, planking, fittings, and other structures that must remain sound on the water.

Narrative effects: You look at vessels as working structures and notice joints, wear, alignment, leaks, and repairs that will become larger problems if ignored.

entries.name: Shopfront Assistant
entries.summary:
You helped in a shopfront, stall, family business, inn counter, or trade room, learning small talk, price pressure, and customer suspicion.

Narrative effects: You size up customers by hands, eyes, clothes, and how long they stare before speaking.

entries.name: Smuggler's Contact
entries.summary:
You served as a contact, lookout, carrier, messenger, safehouse helper, dockside watcher, or quiet middle-person for smugglers.

Narrative effects: You ask what is in the crate, who must not see it, and why it is worth the risk.

entries.name: Spycraft Trainee
entries.summary:
You began training in spycraft: observation, coded messages, dead drops, false names, quiet movement, information gathering, and controlled lies.

Narrative effects: You notice repeated faces, false pauses, reflections, and people who listen too well.

entries.name: Stable Hand
entries.summary:
You worked around horses, mules, draft animals, riding beasts, tack, feed, stalls, grooming, manure, injuries, nervous animals, and people who expected their mounts ready when needed.

Narrative effects: You judge a stable by the animals before you judge it by the people.

entries.name: Still Living at Home
entries.summary:
You entered early adulthood while still living with family, guardians, a household, village caretakers, temple hosts, or the people who raised you. This may mean safety, duty, poverty, affection, control, unfinished business, or simply that leaving has not happened yet.

Narrative effects: You know the comfort and frustration of being grown but not fully gone.

entries.name: Street Survivor Grown Up
entries.summary:
You survived long enough on streets, docks, alleys, poor districts, gangs' edges, or market shadows to enter adulthood with habits that kept you alive.

Narrative effects: You read streets by who owns them, who fears them, and where people disappear.

entries.name: Saved Every Coin
entries.summary:
Whenever you received a coin, token, allowance, payment, gift, or spending money, your first instinct was often to keep it rather than spend it immediately.

Narrative effects: You naturally think about value before spending and are reluctant to exchange something useful without considering what it is worth.

entries.name: Saw Forbidden Magic
entries.summary:
As a child, you witnessed magic adults clearly did not want discussed openly. You may have understood very little at the time, but secrecy surrounding the event made the memory difficult to forget.

Narrative effects: You know that magical practice has boundaries people cross in secret and can recognize some warning signs without automatically knowing the full truth behind what you saw.

entries.name: Secret-Path Finder
entries.summary:
You loved discovering hidden paths, gaps in fences, forgotten passages, creek routes, back stairs, old service corridors, and places adults rarely used.

Narrative effects: You instinctively look for overlooked routes rather than assuming the obvious entrance is the only way through.

entries.name: Shadowed a Craftsperson
entries.summary:
A particular craftsperson fascinated you enough that you repeatedly watched them work, fetched simple things, asked questions, and absorbed the rhythm of the workshop without yet becoming a formal apprentice.

Narrative effects: You recognize the difference between casual handling and practiced workmanship even though childhood observation did not make you a professional craftsperson.

entries.name: Slow but Stubborn Learner
entries.summary:
Some lessons took longer for you than they did for other children, but frustration rarely made you quit. Once you decided to understand something, you kept returning to it.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable examining a problem repeatedly and do not mistake quick understanding for the only form of intelligence.

entries.name: Snow Wanderer
entries.summary:
Snow, frozen paths, winter fields, icy streets, or cold forests became places you explored rather than merely endured. You learned how much familiar terrain could change beneath winter conditions.

Narrative effects: Cold conditions bother you less than most, and you understand how snow and ice alter routes and landmarks.

entries.name: Sailor's Cabin Child
entries.summary:
You spent substantial childhood time in ships' cabins, below decks, or around crews where lines, sails, watches, bells, cramped quarters, and moving decks were ordinary.

Narrative effects: Sail work and the sounds of a working vessel are familiar, though childhood exposure is not the same as professional seamanship.

entries.name: Seaside Dock Child
entries.summary:
Docks, piers, warehouses, cranes, ropes, cargo, shouting workers, boats, carts, and constantly changing waterfront traffic formed your childhood playground.

Narrative effects: Busy working waterfronts feel readable through both sound and movement without this trait assuming you were trained as a sailor.

entries.name: Servant Hall Child
entries.summary:
Servant halls, staff corridors, back stairs, shared meals, laundry rooms, work schedules, and household gossip formed much of your childhood social world.

Narrative effects: You understand both formal household behavior and the information networks that operate behind public rooms.

entries.name: Shepherd Camp Child
entries.summary:
Flocks, pasture, dogs, hills, simple shelters, weather, predators, distant movement, and long periods of watching animals defined your childhood surroundings.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable watching groups of animals over distance and notice when something in their movement or surroundings changes.

entries.name: Shipyard Child
entries.summary:
Hulls, scaffolds, timber, pitch, rope, tools, drydocks, cranes, repairs, and vessels under construction made up much of your childhood environment.

Narrative effects: Ship construction makes intuitive mechanical sense to you, and you have broad familiarity with the manual work involved.

entries.name: Shopfront Helper
entries.summary:
You regularly helped in a shop by watching stock, carrying small purchases, greeting customers, fetching items, tidying displays, or listening while adults discussed prices.

Narrative effects: Ordinary commercial exchanges feel natural, and you instinctively consider both price and physical quality.

entries.name: Shrine Sweeper
entries.summary:
You spent childhood around a small shrine or sacred space, helping keep paths, floors, lamps, offerings, and ordinary devotional spaces tidy.

Narrative effects: Sacred routines feel practical and familiar, and you understand that reverence often depends on ordinary repetitive work.

entries.name: Stable Helper
entries.summary:
You spent childhood around stables, tack rooms, paddocks, carts, mounts, grooms, feed, manure, and the daily routines required to keep working animals healthy and usable.

Narrative effects: Working animals feel familiar, and you developed modest practical confidence around mounts through repeated exposure.

entries.name: Street Lookout
entries.summary:
You often watched for guards, adults, customers, troublemakers, rival children, returning parents, or anyone whose arrival mattered to the people around you.

Narrative effects: You naturally choose positions with good sightlines and know how to observe without making your attention obvious.

entries.name: Shield Bearer
entries.summary:
You specialize in shields as active combat tools: blocking, bracing, deflecting, controlling space, protecting another person, absorbing pressure, and creating openings with the shield itself. Your expertise is more than simply carrying protection.

Narrative effects: You instinctively consider angles of cover, lines of attack, who is exposed, and where a shield can turn danger away rather than merely absorb it.

entries.name: Skirmisher
entries.summary:
You specialize in mobile fighting that avoids remaining fixed in one place. Your training emphasizes quick repositioning, harassment, pursuit, withdrawal, throwing attacks, and using movement to keep heavier opponents from dictating the exchange.

Narrative effects: You prefer fights with room to move and instinctively look for routes that let you strike, relocate, and force an opponent to keep adjusting.

entries.name: Sling Specialist
entries.summary:
You specialize in slings and staff slings, learning the timing, release angle, ammunition choice, range judgment, and practiced rhythm needed to make a simple projectile weapon genuinely dangerous.

Narrative effects: You judge distance, arc, available ammunition, and release timing with the practiced eye of someone who knows how much precision a sling actually demands.

entries.name: Spear Specialist
entries.summary:
You specialize in spears and related thrusting weapons. Your training emphasizes point control, quick redirection, economical footwork, repeated thrusts, defensive spacing, and using reach without becoming slow or predictable.

Narrative effects: You are constantly aware of measure: the exact distance at which your point threatens an opponent while keeping their own attack just short.

entries.name: Staff Specialist
entries.summary:
You specialize in quarterstaffs, battle staffs, and similar two-handed staff weapons. Your training emphasizes leverage, rapid hand transitions, defensive redirection, sweeping control, thrusts, strikes, and keeping both ends of the weapon useful.

Narrative effects: A staff feels less like one weapon than a moving line of leverage; you naturally adjust grip, stance, and angle as distance changes.

entries.name: Swordsmanship Specialist
entries.summary:
You specialize in swords and other dueling blades whose use depends on timing, measure, guard control, footwork, cuts, thrusts, parries, and disciplined weapon handling. Your training favors technical exchanges over simply overpowering an opponent.

Narrative effects: You read guards, foot placement, blade position, tempo, and distance almost automatically when a weapon is drawn.

entries.name: Scholarly Mind
entries.summary:
Your mind strongly favors memory, theory, structured learning, technical reasoning, tactics, and complex practical or magical problems. Grants +8 Intelligence.

Narrative effects: You organize difficult questions into parts, compare them against what you know, and search for a coherent underlying rule.

entries.name: Social Awareness
entries.summary:
You combine awareness, observation, pattern recognition, and subtle cues with presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Perception and +4 Communication.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing awareness, observation, pattern recognition, and subtle cues and presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Steadfast Presence
entries.summary:
Your aptitude strongly favors physical steadiness and endurance, with enough social presence to project reliability rather than merely survive strain. Grants +6 Constitution and +2 Communication.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain, calling on presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Steady Marksman
entries.summary:
Your aptitude strongly favors endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain, while aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement provides a meaningful secondary strength. Grants +6 Constitution and +2 Accuracy.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain, calling on aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Steady Precision
entries.summary:
You combine endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain with aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Constitution and +4 Accuracy.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain and aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Sturdy Physique
entries.summary:
You combine physical power with lasting toughness in nearly equal measure, favoring a body that can both apply force and keep applying it. Grants +4 Strength and +4 Constitution.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing physical power, leverage, and force and endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Sacred Family Tradition
entries.summary:
Generations of your family have served temples, shrines, pilgrim routes, sacred households, burial traditions, religious charities, or other recognized forms of spiritual service. The legacy may inspire devotion, skepticism, duty, resentment, or simply familiarity with sacred expectations.

Narrative effects: You recognize ritual behavior, sacred courtesy, religious reputation, and the social weight carried by families repeatedly trusted with spiritual duties.

entries.name: Sailmaker Family
entries.summary:
Sailmakers, canvas workers, rope-and-cloth repairers, or maritime textile specialists recur through your family history. Measurement, stitching, reinforcement, wear, wind, and emergency repair tied workshop craft directly to life aboard ships.

Narrative effects: You recognize how sails are built, damaged, repaired, and actually used rather than treating them as simple sheets of cloth.

entries.name: Scholarly Family
entries.summary:
Scholars, tutors, archivists, researchers, physicians, teachers, or other learned professionals recur through your family history. Books, correspondence, arguments over evidence, old records, and the expectation that someone should know the answer were ordinary parts of family life.

Narrative effects: You are inclined to ask what the evidence says, who recorded it, and whether the accepted story survived because it was true or merely convenient.

entries.name: Seafaring Family
entries.summary:
Sailors, fishers, navigators, dockworkers, shipwrights, ferrymen, or maritime traders recur through your family's history. Tides, rope, weather, cargo, boats, and stories about people who did not return are part of the family memory.

Narrative effects: You notice wind, current, cargo balance, bad knots, changing weather, and whether someone treating the water casually has ever depended on it.

entries.name: Shepherd's Line
entries.summary:
Shepherds, drovers, herders, flock keepers, or other people responsible for grazing animals recur through your family history. Long watches, difficult births, missing animals, predators, weather, pasture, and patient daily movement became familiar family stories.

Narrative effects: You pay attention to animal behavior and notice movement, separation, danger, and changes across open ground that others may overlook.

entries.name: Shipwright Family
entries.summary:
Shipwrights, boat builders, hull repairers, dockyard carpenters, or other vessel builders recur through your family history. Frames, planks, joints, curves, balance, leaks, and repairs made ships into constructed systems rather than mysterious objects.

Narrative effects: You understand many of the structural decisions hidden inside vessels and the practical craftsmanship required to keep them sound.

entries.name: Shrine Keepers
entries.summary:
Your family repeatedly maintained small shrines, roadside holy places, memorial sites, local sanctuaries, or sacred landmarks. Keeping such places respectable required ritual familiarity as well as cleaning, repairs, offerings, and ordinary practical care.

Narrative effects: You recognize sacred customs and understand that maintaining a holy place often depends on mundane repair and upkeep as much as ceremony.

entries.name: Smithing Dynasty
entries.summary:
Smiths, armorers, weapon makers, farriers, metalworkers, or forge specialists recur throughout your family history. Heat, metal, tools, repairs, apprenticeships, and arguments about proper workmanship have followed the family for generations.

Narrative effects: You look at metalwork for balance, joins, wear, repair marks, and whether the maker cared what happened after the sale.

entries.name: Script Scholar
entries.summary:
You study scripts, handwriting traditions, formal lettering, manuscript hands, historical notation, copied texts, inscriptions, and the visual conventions by which writing changes across places and eras. This does not make every unknown language readable, but it helps identify and reproduce written forms accurately.

Narrative effects: You notice stroke order, hand style, age, copying conventions, alterations, and the historical context suggested by how something was written rather than only what the words say.

entries.name: Supernatural Scholar
entries.summary:
You study supernatural beings and anomalies that do not fit ordinary natural categories, including demons, strange spirits, extraplanar entities, magical manifestations, corrupted beings, and difficult classifications. This expertise helps compare possibilities without declaring every unexplained event forbidden or planar.

Narrative effects: You compare unusual phenomena across known supernatural categories, looking for the origin, rules, boundaries, and evidence that distinguish one kind of entity or anomaly from another.

entries.name: Shadow Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Shadow Arcana: darkness, concealment, silence, suppressed perception, hidden movement, and severed attention. Though often feared, it has ordinary disciplined uses as well as dangerous ones.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable near edges: doorways, dim corners, half-truths, and places where attention slips away.

entries.name: Smoke Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Smoke Arcana: smoke, vapor, haze, breath-clouds, ash-clouds, obscuring air, scent trails, and drifting concealment. Your magic expresses this theme instinctively, and training turns that instinct into controlled spellwork.

Narrative effects: You notice drafts, haze, scent trails, and where smoke would hide a movement.

entries.name: Spirit Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Spirit Arcana: spirits, ghosts, animistic presences, hauntings, ancestor echoes, shrine entities, and unseen local powers. Your magic expresses this theme instinctively, and training turns that instinct into controlled spellwork.

Narrative effects: You notice shrines, old grief, watched silence, and the mood of unseen presences.

entries.name: Solarian Mercy-House
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Solarian healing houses, charitable institutions, temple care, public medicine, and the belief that tending suffering carries moral significance. Healing magic is therefore not merely a specialist's art but one of the most visible magical traditions in the culture.

Narrative effects: You are familiar with Solarian ideals of care and with the human realities surrounding illness and injury. Healing Arcana is culturally learned magical capability; Medicine still represents the practical skill of treatment.

entries.name: Solarian Pilgrim-Road
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Solarian pilgrim roads, shrine routes, charitable stops, traveling congregations, and the constant meeting of people from different regions under a shared religious framework. Healing magic is familiar as both sacred practice and practical mercy along those roads.

Narrative effects: You understand pilgrim customs, routes, hospitality, and the many regional expressions found within Solarian religious life. Healing Arcana reflects the culture's strong association between faith and care.

entries.name: Solarian Temple-City
entries.summary:
You were shaped by the temple-centered life of the Solarian Theocracy, where public ritual, doctrine, sacred institutions, visible morality, and proper conduct influence everyday reputation. Healing magic is among the culture's most respected magical traditions because care of body and community is treated as sacred work.

Narrative effects: You understand Solarian doctrine, public ritual, and the social expectations surrounding visible virtue. Healing Arcana is a culturally respected magical foundation and does not require clerical status.

entries.name: Solmire Contract-Court
entries.summary:
You were shaped by the formal side of Solmire commerce, where contracts, arbitration, polished negotiation, merchant politics, and carefully worded obligations determine who wins without drawing a blade. Rune magic is culturally at home wherever written terms and prepared effects are expected to endure.

Narrative effects: You understand how courtesy, argument, and formal agreement interact in Solmire society. Rune Arcana is a culturally familiar tool of prepared magic, not an automatic legal profession.

entries.name: Solmire Harbor-Market
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Solmire's crowded ports, warehouses, brokers, foreign cargoes, private fleets, and competitive markets. Rune magic remains culturally familiar through marks of ownership, shipping records, seals, contracts, and prepared commercial protections.

Narrative effects: You are practiced at judging goods and negotiating value in busy commercial settings. Rune Arcana represents Solmire's written magical culture rather than a particular trade.

entries.name: Solmire Ledgerwise
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Solmire's ledgers, merchant houses, account books, written obligations, brokers, and the belief that a properly recorded agreement can be more powerful than a shouted promise. Rune magic fits naturally into a culture that values written forms, marks, prepared terms, and durable records.

Narrative effects: You instinctively look for terms, records, witnesses, and what was actually written. Rune Arcana reflects Solmire's cultural use of prepared written magic without making every Solmire native a professional runesmith.

entries.name: Stormpearl Harborhouse
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Stormpearl harbors, pearl trade, island houses, visiting crews, boat law, markets, and communities that depend on exchange across dangerous water. Lightning magic remains part of the islands' cultural identity, as familiar as storm warnings and charged skies.

Narrative effects: You understand island commerce and Stormpearl customs around harbor life, trade, and reputation. Lightning Arcana reflects the islands' magical character without defining your livelihood.

entries.name: Stormpearl Outer-Islander
entries.summary:
You were shaped by smaller or more exposed Stormpearl communities where water separates neighbors, swimming can be practical rather than recreational, and knowing how to reach the next safe shore matters. Lightning magic is part of the same storm-battered cultural environment.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable moving through and around island waters and thinking in routes between separated shores. Lightning Arcana is a cultural inheritance, not a requirement that you grew up as a sailor.

entries.name: Stormpearl Stormwise
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Stormpearl communities where storms, exposed seas, fishing fleets, dangerous weather, and rapid changes in coastal conditions are ordinary facts of life. Lightning magic is the islands' characteristic magical signature, reflecting a culture accustomed to living beneath violent skies.

Narrative effects: You read sea and weather with practical respect and understand the working habits of storm-exposed island communities. Lightning Arcana is culturally familiar magic rather than proof that you command storms professionally.

entries.name: Scout Archer
entries.summary:
You have deliberately learned to combine Stealth and Bows as one working discipline instead of treating them as unrelated skills. The overlap gives you options that depend on both kinds of competence and grants the signature ability Silent Opening.

Narrative effects: Treat Scout Archer as a genuine hybrid specialization. The character combines Stealth with Bows when both materially matter to the approach; do not let either skill substitute for the other or bypass normal tools, authority, resources, evidence, positioning, or consequences.

entries.name: Seal Arcana
entries.summary:
You carry a rare resonance with Seal Arcana, awakened through wards, locked thresholds, forbidden bindings, relic influence, containment pressure, or story consequence. Seal Arcana governs closure, binding marks, locked power, containment, restriction, warded promises, and the force that says something must remain held. It can protect, imprison, preserve, or suppress depending on intent and skill.

Narrative effects: You notice locks, ward lines, closed doors, binding marks, strained barriers, and places where power has been deliberately held back.

entries.name: Seal Arcana Mastery
entries.summary:
You have trained Seal Arcana beyond simple affinity into a major specialization. Your control is more precise, economical, and reliable inside its established domain, but mastery does not expand what the Arcana governs or remove mana costs, opposition, risk, or story consequences. This mastery grants the signature ability Nested Seal.

Narrative effects: Treat Seal Arcana as a major specialization. Favor deliberate, technically informed expressions of the authored Seal Arcana domain; do not reinterpret it as another Arcana, grant effects outside its definition, or waive normal mana, strain, witnesses, and consequences. The character may use Nested Seal when its fictional setup is plausible; it is a mastery technique, not automatic success or permission to exceed the Arcana domain.

entries.name: Searching Apex
entries.summary:
Your command of searching is exceptional even among seasoned specialists. You combine economy, judgement, and control across systematic examination, concealed spaces, subtle physical clues, secret mechanisms, and noticing what does not fit, while still respecting tools, resources, environment, and credible opposition.

Narrative effects: Treat the character as an exceptional searching practitioner. Let expertise change what approaches are plausible, but never erase consequences, impossible geometry, unavailable tools, social authority, or established world rules.

entries.name: Searching Discipline
entries.summary:
You have turned searching into a deliberate specialty through repeated practice. You are reliably trained in systematic examination, concealed spaces, subtle physical clues, secret mechanisms, and noticing what does not fit, but difficult situations still depend on position, tools, opposition, and judgement.

Narrative effects: Treat searching as a practiced specialization. The character deliberately applies systematic examination, concealed spaces, subtle physical clues, secret mechanisms, and noticing what does not fit; give that training weight without granting automatic success or ignoring normal constraints.

entries.name: Searching Expertise
entries.summary:
Your searching remains reliable when conditions become complicated. You can adapt systematic examination, concealed spaces, subtle physical clues, secret mechanisms, and noticing what does not fit to pressure, poor timing, difficult terrain, and active opposition instead of relying on ideal circumstances.

Narrative effects: Treat the character as an experienced searching specialist who adapts technique under pressure. Preserve normal risk, resource costs, physical limits, law, witnesses, and opposition.

entries.name: Searching Mastery
entries.summary:
Searching has become one of your defining masteries. You recognize advanced openings and methods within systematic examination, concealed spaces, subtle physical clues, secret mechanisms, and noticing what does not fit, and this trait grants the signature ability Pattern Break.

Narrative effects: Treat searching as a defining mastery. The character may use Pattern Break when its fictional setup is plausible; it creates a special option, not guaranteed success or permission to bypass unrelated skills.

You helped measure, carry, stitch, patch, fold, stretch, and prepare sails or heavy sailcloth for working vessels.

Narrative effects: You understand the physical construction of sails and how their practical use affects repair and workmanship.

entries.name: Scribe's Ink Grinder
entries.summary:
You prepared ink, trimmed simple writing materials, carried papers, copied short passages, and watched a scribe's work closely enough to practice precise lettering yourself.

Narrative effects: Careful mundane script and ordinary written composition developed through repetitive clerical work.

entries.name: Shepherd's Helper
entries.summary:
You regularly helped watch, gather, feed, move, or count sheep, goats, or similar livestock over open ground.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable directing herd animals and watching their movement across distance.

entries.name: Shipyard Runner
entries.summary:
You carried tools, parts, messages, food, measurements, or instructions between workers around a busy shipyard.

Narrative effects: Ship construction environments and moving efficiently through large work sites feel familiar.

entries.name: Shop Ledger Helper
entries.summary:
You helped copy entries, locate old transactions, organize receipts, check simple records, and keep shop paperwork legible.

Narrative effects: Finding information in business records and producing clear precise script feel familiar.

entries.name: Shrine Acolyte
entries.summary:
You assisted with lamps, offerings, visitors, simple ceremonies, cleaning, preparation, and the small formalities surrounding a shrine.

Narrative effects: Religious customs and respectful ceremonial behavior feel practiced rather than merely observed.

entries.name: Shrine Donation Counter
entries.summary:
You helped sort offerings, count coins, inspect donated goods, record simple gifts, or prepare contributions for storage and use.

Narrative effects: You understand both the material value and religious context of ordinary offerings.

entries.name: Sibling Minder
entries.summary:
You were regularly expected to supervise a younger sibling, cousin, wardmate, or other child and make basic decisions when adults were occupied.

Narrative effects: You are accustomed to reading a younger person's needs while also being the one expected to decide what happens next.

entries.name: Smithy Bellows Child
entries.summary:
You pumped bellows, carried fuel, fetched tools, moved simple materials, and endured the heat and noise of a working smithy.

Narrative effects: Basic forge processes and genuine physical exposure to sustained heat are familiar, though you were not yet a master smith.

entries.name: Soldier's Runner
entries.summary:
You regularly carried messages, equipment, food, or requests for soldiers, guards, officers, or military staff.

Narrative effects: Military organization and moving information quickly through it are familiar responsibilities.

entries.name: Stable Rider
entries.summary:
Stable work became a regular responsibility, and you were trusted not only to groom, feed, and lead mounts but also to ride them for short practical tasks.

Narrative effects: Working with mounts and controlling them during ordinary riding are familiar responsibilities.

entries.name: Stage Costume Helper
entries.summary:
You helped performers change clothing, arrange costumes, apply simple alterations, prepare appearances, and make people look convincingly unlike their everyday selves.

Narrative effects: Changing appearance through clothing and presentation feels familiar from theatrical work rather than espionage.

entries.name: Street Errand Runner
entries.summary:
You earned favors, food, coins, or simple approval by running messages and small deliveries through busy streets for whoever needed quick feet.

Narrative effects: Urban routes become familiar quickly, and you are practiced at moving efficiently between destinations.

entries.name: Sat Through a Death Vigil
entries.summary:
You remained present through a vigil for someone dying or recently dead, sharing the waiting, rituals, silence, prayers, stories, or practical customs surrounding death.

Narrative effects: You are familiar with ritual responses to death and with the patience required simply to remain present through grief.

entries.name: Saved for Something Important
entries.summary:
You denied yourself smaller wants for long enough to save toward something that genuinely mattered to you.

Narrative effects: You learned to delay immediate gratification and think carefully about whether something is worth what it costs.

entries.name: Saw a Dragon Overhead
entries.summary:
You saw a dragon in the distance or passing overhead clearly enough that the encounter became one of the defining sights of your preteen years.

Narrative effects: The encounter drove you to learn more about dragons and left you attentive to the details by which they might be recognized.

entries.name: Saw a Great City
entries.summary:
You visited a city large enough that its crowds, districts, walls, markets, institutions, roads, and social variety changed your sense of how many ways people could live.

Narrative effects: Large settlements feel less overwhelming, and you understand that urban life contains many overlapping communities and routes.

entries.name: Secret Keeper
entries.summary:
Someone entrusted you with a secret whose consequences were serious enough that keeping it became a defining lesson rather than ordinary childhood discretion.

Narrative effects: You understand both the emotional weight of being trusted and the practical difficulty of concealing important information.

entries.name: Secret Language Learner
entries.summary:
You learned a cipher, coded script, hidden shorthand, substitution system, secret signs, or another deliberate method of communicating information that outsiders were not meant to understand.

Narrative effects: Encoding and decoding information became a real learned skill, supported by careful control of written symbols.

entries.name: Shadowed by a Stranger
entries.summary:
For a time, you became convinced that an unfamiliar person was following, observing, or repeatedly appearing near you. Whether the threat was real or misunderstood, you learned to watch back.

Narrative effects: Repeated faces and suspicious movement stand out to you, and you know how to reduce your own visibility when necessary.

entries.name: Smuggled Food to Someone
entries.summary:
You secretly brought food, water, medicine, or another basic necessity to someone who was being denied it or could not safely obtain it themselves.

Narrative effects: You learned that compassion sometimes requires acting quietly when authority, circumstance, or social pressure stands in the way.

entries.name: Survived a Border Raid
entries.summary:
A raid struck your settlement, road, camp, or surrounding region while you were old enough to understand what was happening.

Narrative effects: Firsthand exposure taught you how raids, defenses, armed movement, warnings, and vulnerable approaches actually look without making you a trained soldier.

entries.name: Survived a Fire
entries.summary:
You survived a serious fire while old enough to understand the danger, whether in a home, workshop, street, field, forest, ship, or other place.

Narrative effects: Real exposure to heat and smoke left you physically hardened and attentive to visible signs of spreading fire.

entries.name: Survived a Monster Sighting
entries.summary:
You encountered or clearly saw a dangerous creature closely enough that the experience changed monsters from stories into real threats.

Narrative effects: You pay attention to the physical signs and behavior of unusual creatures without one encounter making you a professional monster hunter.

entries.name: Survived a Winter Shortage
entries.summary:
A difficult winter brought genuine shortages of food, fuel, medicine, shelter, or other essentials, and you were old enough to understand how carefully everything had to be rationed.

Narrative effects: Real physical deprivation made you more resistant to harsh conditions and more conscious of the value of basic supplies.

entries.name: Swore Temple Oath
entries.summary:
You deliberately swore an oath in a temple, shrine, sacred place, or before a religious authority. The oath may have been temporary, personal, ceremonial, or deeply serious.

Narrative effects: You understand the ritual and social seriousness surrounding sacred promises without this trait requiring lifelong devotion.

entries.name: Sailmaker
entries.summary:
You are professionally experienced at measuring, cutting, sewing, reinforcing, repairing, and fitting sails and other heavy working canvas. Your craft depends on understanding both material strain and how sails are actually used aboard vessels.

Narrative effects: You inspect stitching, panels, corners, reef points, wear, stretch, and the direction of load before deciding whether canvas can be patched or must be replaced.

entries.name: Sailor
entries.summary:
You are experienced in ordinary shipboard work: sails, rigging, ropes, anchors, cargo, deck movement, watches, weather response, small boats, and the routines that keep a vessel functioning. This does not automatically make you the vessel's navigator or captain.

Narrative effects: You react to changing wind, shifting decks, loose lines, damaged rigging, cargo movement, and shouted shipboard orders with the habits of someone who has worked afloat.

entries.name: Scribe
entries.summary:
You are professionally practiced at drafting, copying, formatting, preserving, and handling written documents. Letters, petitions, contracts, ledgers, formal notices, copied manuscripts, and institutional records benefit from your control of language and careful script.

Narrative effects: You notice handwriting, ink, spacing, seals, copying errors, revisions, and whether a document looks like the work of someone who understood the form they were using.

entries.name: Shepherd
entries.summary:
You are experienced at managing grazing animals through feeding, movement, weather, injury, predators, breeding seasons, and difficult terrain. Shepherding combines practical animal control with strong awareness of pasture and local natural conditions.

Narrative effects: You count animals automatically, notice changes in gait or appetite, watch weather and grazing pressure, and pay attention when the flock reacts to something before people do.

entries.name: Shipbuilder
entries.summary:
You are professionally experienced in constructing and repairing ships and boats: hull structure, frames, planking, joints, sealing, fittings, weight distribution, and the practical relationship between a vessel's design and the water it must survive. This is ordinary shipbuilding expertise, distinct from the advanced Shipwright hybrid specialization.

Narrative effects: You look at hull lines, framing, seams, repairs, load, balance, rot, and stress before trusting a vessel or deciding how a damaged one can safely be restored.

entries.name: Spycraft Operative
entries.summary:
You are professionally trained in covert information work: surveillance, countersurveillance, discreet meetings, informants, dead drops, coded signals, false identities, observation, and handling sensitive information without drawing unnecessary attention.

Narrative effects: You look for tails, repeated faces, unusual pauses, compromised meeting places, concealed exchanges, and the procedures by which secrets are moved rather than merely spoken.

entries.name: Stablemaster
entries.summary:
You are experienced in the daily management of mounts and stable animals: feeding, grooming, tack, stalls, exercise, basic condition checks, work schedules, handling, and keeping animals ready for travel or service.

Narrative effects: You notice poor tack fit, neglected hooves, uneven feeding, nervous stalls, tired mounts, and whether an animal is genuinely ready for the work someone expects from it.

entries.name: Steward
entries.summary:
You understand the practical management of households, estates, farms, stores, servants, repairs, schedules, local obligations, and recurring operational problems. Stewardship is the work of keeping resources, people, and responsibilities aligned before neglect becomes crisis.

Narrative effects: You notice empty stores, delayed work, tired staff, neglected maintenance, unclear responsibility, and small failures that will become expensive if nobody owns them.

entries.name: Serpentfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Serpentfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus slit pupils, subtle scale-pattern markings, smooth movement, cool skin tone, and snake-like eyes. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Scent-sensitive perception, still posture, smooth movement, and tactile awareness favor quiet observation and unobtrusive movement. Serpentfolk are not inherently deceitful, cold, manipulative, or malicious.

entries.name: Sharkfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Sharkfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus shark-like eyes, sharp human teeth, finlike markings, subtle rough skin texture, and water-ready posture. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: A water-ready build, rougher skin texture, strong scent sensitivity, and aquatic instincts favor powerful swimming and endurance in water. Do not grant underwater breathing or predatory aggression unless another mechanic establishes it.

entries.name: Sheepfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Sheepfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus sheep ears, woolly hair, soft features, possible small horns, and a body naturally insulated by dense hair. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Dense woolly hair, sensitive hearing, scent awareness, and steady physical endurance help with exposure and environmental awareness. Gentleness, passivity, pastoral work, handcrafting, and obedience are not racial requirements.

entries.name: Spiritfolk
entries.summary:
Spiritfolk are living mortal people whose lineage has been shaped by spirits, old shrines, ancestor pacts, nature forces, local gods, or other persistent contact with the unseen world. Their exact manifestation is intentionally broad and may include luminous eyes, unusual markings, strange hair, omen-like sensations, or a subtle spiritual presence. They are not ghosts, undead, or automatically religious.

Narrative effects: Your lineage carries a real Spirit affinity, but the source and meaning of that inheritance remain open to the character concept unless established elsewhere. This trait does not grant prophecy, a spirit companion, priestly authority, or a mandatory pact.

entries.name: Squirrelfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Squirrelfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus squirrel ears, a large fluffy tail, quick feet, bright eyes, and agile hands. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Strong climbing instincts, fast balance corrections, quick hands, and a large expressive tail favor vertical movement and delicate manipulation. Hoarding or nervousness may be habits, never mandatory racial behavior.

entries.name: Storyteller
entries.summary:
You specialize in telling stories aloud through pacing, characterization, memory, dramatic emphasis, and awareness of the traditions an audience recognizes. Your stories may entertain, teach, preserve memory, persuade indirectly, or simply make people listen.

Narrative effects: You instinctively shape a tale around the moments an audience will remember and the references they will understand.

entries.name: Streetwise Operator
entries.summary:
You know how to navigate informal social power in commoner districts, taverns, docks, gangs, black markets, rough neighborhoods, and criminal-adjacent circles. You read who belongs, who controls access, where information moves, and which unwritten rules matter more than the posted ones.

Narrative effects: You look for the person everyone casually checks before deciding whether a stranger is welcome.

entries.name: Sailor's Clothes Set
entries.summary: Clothing suited for ships, docks, rope work, wet decks, salt air, and hard weather. Built to move, dry, and survive rough handling.

entries.name: Scholar's Robes Set
entries.summary: Robes suited for libraries, tutors, archives, academies, and long hours with ink-stained hands. They suggest study before status.

entries.name: Servant's Uniform Set
entries.summary: A clean but modest uniform suited for household service, kitchens, halls, stables, and noble residences. It marks the wearer as useful, expected, and often underestimated.

entries.name: Smith's Apron Set
entries.summary: Heavy workshop wear with an apron suited for sparks, soot, tools, hot metal, and long hours near a forge.

entries.name: Stealth Clothing Set
entries.summary: Dark, quiet, close-fitting clothing suited for night movement, rooftops, hidden paths, and situations where loose fabric or bright color would betray you.

entries.name: Street Urchin Clothes Set
entries.summary: Layered scraps, patched sleeves, hidden pockets, and clothing chosen for movement through alleys rather than respectability. It belongs to someone used to being overlooked.

entries.name: Scale Armor Set
entries.summary: Armor made from overlapping metal, horn, or hardened plates arranged like scales. It offers solid protection while retaining some flexibility.

entries.name: Stealth Armor Set
entries.summary: Dark, flexible armor designed to protect without clattering, catching light, or restricting silent movement. Favored by scouts, infiltrators, spies, and night fighters.

entries.name: Studded Leather Armor Set
entries.summary: Reinforced leather armor set with metal studs, plates, or hardened sections worked into vulnerable areas. It offers a stronger defense while staying lighter than mail.

entries.name: Sap Gloves
entries.summary: Weighted gloves designed to make close punches land harder while keeping the hands free.

entries.name: Shepherd's Sling
entries.summary: Starting weapon for Slings. A plain cord sling used by herders, scouts, and v.

entries.name: Short Spear
entries.summary: A compact thrusting spear suited for guards, hunters, and close formation work in tight spaces.

entries.name: Short Sword
entries.summary: A compact blade suited for guards, scouts, close quarters, narrow alleys, ship decks, and practical sidearm use. Easier to carry than a longsword and more reliable than a knife in a real fight.

entries.name: Shortbow
entries.summary: A compact bow suited for hunters, scouts, mounted riders, and travelers who need a ranged weapon that is easier to carry than a longbow.

entries.name: Shuriken
entries.summary: Starting weapon for Thrown Weapons. A small bladed star designed for distraction, har.

entries.name: Small Shield
entries.summary: A compact shield suited for travel, skirmishing, light defense, and quick repositioning. Easier to carry than larger shields and still much better than bare forearms.

entries.name: Smallsword
entries.summary: A light thrusting blade suited for formal duels, quick footwork, and precise courtly violence.

entries.name: Spear
entries.summary: A simple, reliable thrusting weapon with reach enough to keep danger at bay. Favored by guards, soldiers, hunters, villagers, and anyone who understands the value of not letting claws get close.

entries.name: Spiked Gauntlets
entries.summary: Starting weapon for Brawling. Heavy gauntlets with short spikes for brutal clos.

entries.name: Staff Sling
entries.summary: Starting weapon for Slings. A long sling fixed to a staff, trading speed for.

entries.name: Steel Dagger
entries.summary: A sharp steel dagger useful as a sidearm, tool, concealed weapon, or last resort. Small blades are rarely honorable, but they are often close enough when honor is not.

entries.name: Stiletto
entries.summary: A narrow thrusting dagger designed for precision and concealment rather than broad cutting force.

entries.name: Stone Sling
entries.summary: A plain cord sling for common stones, easy to carry and dangerous only in trained hands.

entries.name: Secret Engagement
entries.summary:
You and another person privately agreed to marry, bind yourselves together, or pursue a future that could not yet be acknowledged openly.

Narrative effects: You learned to conceal a socially significant relationship while understanding the formal expectations surrounding it. It need not remain active today.

entries.name: Servant With Noble Secrets
entries.summary:
Service around nobles or other high-status people exposed you to conversations, habits, private relationships, disputes, or other facts that were never intended for wider circulation.

Narrative effects: You understand how much servants can learn simply by being present and how carefully high-status privacy must be navigated.

entries.name: Sold Out by Friends
entries.summary:
People you considered friends deliberately exposed, betrayed, blamed, abandoned, or traded information about you when doing so benefited them.

Narrative effects: Betrayal taught you to read relationships more carefully and recognize how convincing false loyalty can appear.

entries.name: Survived a Monster Attack
entries.summary:
A dangerous creature genuinely attacked you or a group you were part of, turning monsters from distant stories into immediate physical threats.

Narrative effects: The attack taught you to function around frightening creatures and gave you some firsthand understanding of their behavior.

entries.name: Survived a Raid
entries.summary:
A military, bandit, pirate, tribal, or factional raid struck somewhere you lived, traveled, or worked during your teenage years.

Narrative effects: Firsthand exposure taught you how raids unfold and what it feels like to act while armed violence is happening nearby.

entries.name: Survived a Siege
entries.summary:
You lived through a prolonged siege involving confinement, shortages, uncertainty, disease risk, bombardment, repeated alarms, or physical deprivation.

Narrative effects: You understand siege conditions firsthand, and genuine prolonged physical hardship left you somewhat more resistant to harsh conditions.

entries.name: Swore a Serious Oath
entries.summary:
During your teenage years, you deliberately made a promise you understood to carry genuine personal, social, religious, or political weight.

Narrative effects: You learned how serious commitments shape behavior and how formal promises are recognized by others. The trait does not require that the oath remains active.

entries.name: Sailmaker's Apprentice
entries.summary:
You trained to measure, cut, stitch, reinforce, repair, and prepare sails while learning how shape, tension, and damage affected their use aboard vessels.

Narrative effects: Sail construction became a serious craft skill supported by practical understanding of how sails behave in use.

entries.name: Sailor's Deckhand
entries.summary:
You served regularly aboard a working vessel, handling sails, lines, deck duties, watches, cleaning, loading, and enough helm work to understand how the vessel responded.

Narrative effects: You developed substantial practical seamanship and useful familiarity with controlling a vessel.

entries.name: Scholarship Student
entries.summary:
Your education depended on a scholarship, sponsorship, examination result, charitable grant, patron, or another opportunity earned rather than automatically available to you.

Narrative effects: You learned to take formal study seriously because continued access depended on sustained academic performance.

entries.name: Self-Taught Reader
entries.summary:
Much of what you learned during adolescence came from your own reading rather than formal instruction. You followed whatever books, stories, histories, borrowed texts, and available records caught your attention.

Narrative effects: Independent reading gave you broad knowledge of peoples and the past, though your education may be uneven where materials were unavailable.

entries.name: Shepherd Teen
entries.summary:
You spent adolescence regularly responsible for flocks or herds over pasture, hills, roads, and open country, often working with limited supervision.

Narrative effects: Managing animals and noticing changes across open terrain became deeply practiced parts of your working life.

entries.name: Shipwright's Apprentice
entries.summary:
You trained around hulls, frames, planking, repairs, structural joins, drydocks, tools, and the practical geometry required to keep a vessel sound.

Narrative effects: Ship construction gave you strong practical engineering knowledge supported by substantial manual craft experience.

entries.name: Shopfront Heir
entries.summary:
A shop or small business was expected to become partly or fully your responsibility someday, so adolescence included real exposure to prices, stock, customers, quality, and daily commercial decisions.

Narrative effects: You understand the daily commercial decisions involved in keeping a small business functioning. This does not require that you actually inherited it.

entries.name: Shrine Guard Trainee
entries.summary:
You trained to protect a shrine, temple, monastery, sacred procession, religious community, or other holy place where restraint and dependable defense mattered.

Narrative effects: You developed a defensive martial foundation using controlled staff work and shield discipline.

entries.name: Smuggler's Helper
entries.summary:
You assisted people moving prohibited, untaxed, stolen, hidden, or politically sensitive goods across roads, borders, waterways, checkpoints, or local jurisdictions.

Narrative effects: You understand common smuggling practices and learned the importance of routes that avoid unwanted attention.

entries.name: Stayed Home to Help
entries.summary:
Instead of leaving for training, adventure, travel, or an obvious career path, you spent much of adolescence helping keep your household, family business, farm, workshop, or community functioning.

Narrative effects: Years of dependable work taught persistence and broad practical competence without locking you into a specific profession.

entries.name: Street Fighter Teen
entries.summary:
Repeated fights in streets, yards, alleys, workplaces, informal rings, or rough social environments became a significant part of your teenage life.

Narrative effects: Close-quarters fighting became a genuine practical skill supported by familiarity with compact blades. The path does not inherently make you criminal.

entries.name: Street Survivor
entries.summary:
Much of adolescence revolved around finding food, shelter, work, safe sleeping places, useful scraps, and ways to avoid becoming an easy target in difficult urban surroundings.

Narrative effects: You became highly practiced at finding overlooked necessities and moving through urban spaces without attracting unnecessary attention.

entries.name: Separated From First Caregiver
entries.summary:
Someone who had been central to your earliest care disappeared from your daily life while you were still very young. Death, travel, imprisonment, illness, separation, reassignment, evacuation, or another circumstance may have caused the break.

Narrative effects: You react strongly to abrupt separations and understand that familiar people can vanish from ordinary life without warning.

entries.name: Separated by Authority
entries.summary:
While still very young, you were separated from a caregiver, sibling, household, or other familiar person because an authority relocated, reassigned, detained, displaced, or otherwise divided the people responsible for your care.

Narrative effects: You understand that forced separation can turn family history into incomplete names, locations, and questions. This trait does not determine whether reunion is possible.

entries.name: Servant-Raised Toddler
entries.summary:
Servants, attendants, maids, cooks, nurses, or household staff shaped your earliest care. You may have belonged to a noble household, temple, inn, estate, or wealthy home, but the people who raised you worked for their living.

Narrative effects: You notice working hands, tired feet, and the people who keep households alive from the background.

entries.name: Sheltered Nursery
entries.summary:
You were kept safe, watched, protected, and separated from rougher parts of the world. Your earliest environment was controlled by people who believed innocence, status, health, or secrecy required walls.

Narrative effects: You notice danger a little late, but you also notice when safety is being carefully staged.

entries.name: Sickly Toddler
entries.summary:
You were a fragile toddler: fevered, weak, slow to recover, or constantly watched by worried caretakers. Illness shaped the way adults treated you and the way you learned to read concern.

Narrative effects: You notice coughs, fever, exhaustion, and the fear people hide around the ill.

entries.name: Silken Cradle
entries.summary:
Your earliest years were wrapped in comfort: good blankets, warm rooms, careful attendants, fine clothes, and enough security that hardship felt distant.

Narrative effects: You notice fine fabric, soft bedding, perfume, and the quiet confidence of wealth.

entries.name: Survived Bandits
entries.summary:
Bandits, raiders, thieves, or violent opportunists threatened your childhood. You survived fear, flight, hiding, loss, or the knowledge that roads are never neutral.

Narrative effects: Roadside silence and too-friendly strangers make you wary.

entries.name: Survived a Bad Fall
entries.summary:
You suffered or narrowly survived a serious fall from stairs, roof, tree, wall, cliff path, window, or another height while still a toddler. Adults remembered the event long after you healed.

Narrative effects: You respect height and footing but are familiar with managing fear around vertical movement.

entries.name: Survived a Fever
entries.summary:
A serious fever nearly took you in your toddler years. Someone watched, prayed, cooled your skin, brewed remedies, or feared the worst until you survived.

Narrative effects: You take sickness seriously, even when others try to shrug it off.

entries.name: Survived a Flood
entries.summary:
Floodwater overtook your home, settlement, road, or shelter while you were still very young. You survived rising water, cold, evacuation, or being carried through conditions adults struggled to control.

Narrative effects: You respect moving water and physical exposure to cold, wet conditions rather than treating floods as merely dramatic scenery.

entries.name: Survived a Harsh Winter
entries.summary:
Your first years included a winter severe enough to threaten food, warmth, travel, livestock, or life itself. Cold and scarcity became part of the household stories surrounding your infancy.

Narrative effects: You take cold exposure, seasonal conditions, stored supplies, and worsening weather seriously before comfort becomes danger.

entries.name: Survived a House Fire
entries.summary:
A serious fire threatened the building or household around you while you were still very young. Smoke, heat, shouting, evacuation, destruction, or the sight of familiar rooms changed by flame became part of your earliest history.

Narrative effects: You pay close attention to visible signs of fire and danger and are accustomed to the idea that a safe place can become unsafe very quickly.

entries.name: Survived a Shipwreck
entries.summary:
A vessel carrying you wrecked, sank, grounded, or broke apart while you were still very young. You survived the water and confusion through rescue, luck, preparation, or the actions of others.

Narrative effects: You understand that vessels can fail suddenly and are less likely to panic when survival depends on acting in water.

entries.name: Sang Before Speaking
entries.summary:
Melody, humming, repeated notes, and little songs came to you before clear conversation did. Adults remembered you making music out of sounds before using them normally.

Narrative effects: Melody and vocal rhythm come naturally, even when you have never formally trained as a musician.

entries.name: Shared Everything
entries.summary:
Food, toys, blankets, interesting stones, stolen spoons, and anything else you considered yours were often offered to other people without much hesitation.

Narrative effects: Offering something tangible remains one of your instinctive ways of building trust or easing tension.

entries.name: Silent Little Shadow
entries.summary:
You followed people quietly, appeared in rooms unnoticed, and learned how to stay near interesting activity without drawing much attention to yourself.

Narrative effects: Moving quietly and watching from the edge of activity still comes naturally to you.

entries.name: Slept Outdoors Easily
entries.summary:
Grass, wagons, porches, camp blankets, hay, boats, and open air could put you to sleep almost as readily as a proper bed.

Narrative effects: Ordinary outdoor discomforts rarely prevent you from settling down when rest is needed.

entries.name: Slept Through Noise
entries.summary:
Crowded rooms, storms, wagons, shouting, animals, music, and household activity rarely disturbed you once you were asleep. Your ability to settle seemed almost stubborn.

Narrative effects: Background disturbance rarely unsettles you as much as it does people who need perfect calm.

entries.name: Slow to Warm Up
entries.summary:
New people, places, foods, situations, and routines usually required time before you accepted them. Once comfortable, however, you could become deeply attached.

Narrative effects: You tend to observe people before trusting them and are comfortable letting relationships develop gradually.

entries.name: Sorted Everything
entries.summary:
You arranged toys, stones, food, scraps, buttons, shells, or household objects into little groups according to rules only you fully understood.

Narrative effects: You naturally notice differences in material, quality, shape, purpose, and how objects fit into practical categories.

entries.name: Stared at Maps
entries.summary:
Maps, route sketches, painted coastlines, city plans, and strange symbols representing places held your attention before you properly understood what they meant.

Narrative effects: Representations of space make intuitive sense to you, and you enjoy connecting maps with actual routes and places.

entries.name: Stared at Weapons
entries.summary:
Swords, spears, bows, shields, armor, knives, or other weapons fascinated you visually. You watched their shapes, materials, and the way adults handled them.

Narrative effects: Weapons catch your eye as objects with construction, purpose, and social meaning. Merely staring at them as a toddler did not teach you weapon technique.

entries.name: Strange Dreams in the Cradle
entries.summary:
You woke laughing, crying, staring, whispering, or reaching toward things no one else could see. Adults remembered your dreams as unusually vivid even if there was never anything supernatural about them.

Narrative effects: Your inner life remains vivid, and you are accustomed to sorting intense feelings and impressions after waking. This trait does not establish prophetic or magical dreams.

entries.name: Stubborn About Routines
entries.summary:
Meals happened a certain way, familiar objects belonged in familiar places, bedtime followed particular steps, and unexpected changes could provoke stubborn resistance.

Narrative effects: Routines, rituals, and established ways of doing things are easy for you to learn and maintain.

entries.name: Scholarly Pursuits
entries.summary:
You spent serious time with books, tutors, archives, lectures, copied texts, difficult questions, or structured self-study. The discipline trained you to gather, retain, and organize information. Grants +2 Intelligence and +1 Willpower.

Narrative effects: You break unfamiliar questions into parts, compare sources, and keep working when the answer is buried rather than obvious.

entries.name: Sensory Training
entries.summary:
You deliberately sharpened how you use sight, hearing, and systematic attention, practicing the difference between merely looking and actually noticing. Grants +2 Perception and +1 Accuracy.

Narrative effects: You scan deliberately, separate important details from background noise, and revisit places where something feels visually or audibly inconsistent.

entries.name: Situational Awareness
entries.summary:
You trained yourself to maintain awareness while busy, threatened, or surrounded by competing stimuli, keeping track of movement and changes around you. Grants +2 Perception and +1 Fighting.

Narrative effects: You periodically refresh your sense of who is nearby, what has moved, which exits remain open, and where attention is suddenly concentrating.

entries.name: Social Graces
entries.summary:
You were deliberately trained in manners, introductions, tone, deference, confidence, apology, and the many small behaviors that make social interaction smoother when status matters. Grants +2 Communication and +1 Dexterity.

Narrative effects: You adjust posture, tone, formality, and conversational distance quickly once you understand the social setting.

entries.name: Social Maneuvering Practice
entries.summary:
You practiced indirect social pressure, selective truth, reading reactions, and moving through conversations where motives are not stated openly. Grants +2 Communication and +1 Perception.

Narrative effects: You watch reactions as closely as words and are comfortable changing approach when a person reveals more through hesitation or interest than through a direct answer.

entries.name: Sparring Practice
entries.summary:
You spent sustained time in controlled fights, learning timing, openings, pressure, recovery from mistakes, and how another person actually moves when resisting you. Grants +2 Fighting and +1 Dexterity.

Narrative effects: You read shoulders, hips, reach, rhythm, and hesitation in close exchanges instead of treating combat as a sequence of isolated attacks.

entries.name: Strategic Study
entries.summary:
You studied campaigns, logistics, terrain, formations, historical decisions, and the reasons organized forces succeed or fail. Grants +2 Intelligence and +1 Communication.

Narrative effects: You instinctively ask what each side wants, what resources they possess, what terrain permits, and which decisions will create second-order consequences.

entries.name: Strength Conditioning
entries.summary:
You deliberately trained raw strength through lifting, resistance work, climbing, labor, or repeated force drills. The training develops powerful leverage without assuming a particular profession or fighting style. Grants +2 Strength and +1 Constitution.

Narrative effects: You instinctively look for leverage, stable footing, and the most efficient way to put your whole body behind a difficult physical task.

entries.name: Scholar's Household
entries.summary:
Books, records, correspondence, lessons, arguments over sources, old histories, and scholarly work surrounded you while growing up. Learning was ordinary household activity rather than something encountered only in formal schooling.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable locating written evidence and placing information within a larger historical context.

entries.name: Seaside Village
entries.summary:
You were raised beside the sea in a community shaped by tides, beaches, boats, coastal weather, nearby waters, departures, returns, and the practical risks of living where land ends.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable in water and familiar with using landmarks, coastlines, weather, and direction to orient yourself.

entries.name: Servant Household
entries.summary:
Your household made its living through domestic, estate, court, institutional, or personal service. Schedules, guests, employers, privacy, rank, household routines, and other people's needs were familiar concerns.

Narrative effects: You notice household expectations, proper conduct, mood, discomfort, and the difference between being present and being socially included.

entries.name: Shipboard Raised
entries.summary:
A ship or succession of working vessels served as home for a substantial part of your upbringing. Deck work, helm orders, sails, lines, weather, watches, cramped quarters, ports, and constant movement were ordinary.

Narrative effects: You possess genuine familiarity with practical sail work and directing a vessel, though later professional mastery still requires further experience.

entries.name: Shipyard Settlement
entries.summary:
You were raised around shipyards, drydocks, hulls, timber, rope, cranes, scaffolds, pitch, repair crews, shipwrights, and vessels in various stages of construction.

Narrative effects: You understand the constructed systems behind vessels and possess broad familiarity with the manual work required to build and repair them.

entries.name: Shopkeeper Household
entries.summary:
You grew up behind or above a shop where stock, suppliers, customers, prices, shortages, credit, quality, displays, damaged goods, and daily transactions shaped household life.

Narrative effects: You understand ordinary buying and selling and are accustomed to judging the quality and market worth of physical goods.

entries.name: Street Raised
entries.summary:
A substantial part of your childhood was spent living, working, sleeping, wandering, or surviving in streets and public spaces rather than within a stable household. Crowds, alleys, markets, guards, weather, and constant movement shaped your habits.

Narrative effects: You are practiced at moving unnoticed and moving quickly without this trait automatically making you a thief.
